text:
maria_pm: Quick sync — we need a short decision on streaming semantics for chat/completions before EOW. Customers pushing for resume + lower bandwidth modes.

alex_eng: Can we list the hard constraints? latency SLOs, client complexity, SDK churn, and compatibility with Dedicated/Private.

maria_pm: Yes. For prioritization: 1) predictable finish reasons for consumers 2) graceful fallback if resume state missing 3) minimal SDK changes for simple use-cases.

ranjit_ml: From model/runtime side: resume requires keeping KV checkpoints + stable model variant IDs. That increases state to persist per session. Works, but ops cost increases.

olga_devex: SDK impact note: two transports (SSE and WS) both feasible. SSE simpler for HTTP clients, but harder to support multiplexing and binary deltas. WS gives bidirectional control, easier backpressure signals.

jordan_cs: Customer ask: enterprise customers want resume + deterministic finish reasons so they can reconcile logs with transcripts. They'd prefer WS if we promise reconnection semantics.

alex_eng: Tradeoffs: SSE = easier for server push, natural fallback to chunked HTTP; WS = supports resuming with session token and byte-or-token offsets, but we need clear handshake.

maria_pm: Proposed MVP scope: - support SSE for simple streaming with deltas and explicit finish reasons - support WS only for resume & advanced backpressure in beta (not GA) - canonical delta: JSON lines with {"type": "delta", "delta": "..."} and an explicit final message {"type":"done","finish_reason":"..."}.

ranjit_ml: Concern: JSON-lines adds ambiguity when structured outputs (tool calls, function args) stream partial JSON objects. We should include a framing field like `chunk_id` and `path` for structured streams. Example:
```
{ "type": "delta", "chunk_id": 42, "path": ["choices",0,"message","content"], "delta": "..." }
{ "type": "done", "finish_reason": "stop" }
```
This keeps clients from reassembling wrong fields.

olga_devex: +1 on path framing. Also suggest `resume_token` semantics for WS: server issues `resume_token` every N deltas; on reconnect client sends last-seen token to resume. No heavy per-message seq numbers.

jordan_cs: Need clear launch criteria customers can rely on: 1) finish reason semantics documented 2) SDK helpers for reassembly (JS/Python) 3) canary with 2 enterprise customers + internal load test.

alex_eng: Ops acceptance: Dedicated/private must be able to opt out of resume (state retention) via config. Also cache pruning policy documented.

maria_pm: Decision call: do we go GA with both SSE+WS or GA SSE + WS beta? Poll: react with :one: for GA both, :two: for SSE GA + WS beta.

alex_eng: :two:

ranjit_ml: :two: (WS resume needs more infra testing)

olga_devex: :two: (SDK work to cover resume and structured framing)

jordan_cs: :two: but we should fast-track WS docs for customers who want it early.

maria_pm: Consensus = :two:. Action items: 1) alex to draft handshake + finish_reason enum (by Tue) 2) olga to prototype JS reassembly helper (POC by Wed) 3) ranjit to specify resume_token cadence + storage impact (by Thu) 4) jordan to recruit 2 enterprise customers for WS beta (by Thu).

alex_eng: Quick note on finish_reason enum proposal: `stop`, `length`, `incomplete`, `error`, `cancel`. `incomplete` reserved for resumed/partial sessions.

ranjit_ml: I'll add `resume_token` TTL recommendations and a maximum resume window (e.g., 5 minutes / 1000 tokens) to limit state.

olga_devex: For SDKs: expose a `StreamReassembler` that accepts framed deltas and emits stable message objects; fallback to naive concat for simple streams.

maria_pm: Great. I'll update roadmap entry: "Streaming: SSE GA (deltas + finish reasons + structured framing). WS resume/backpressure beta (resume_token, reassembly SDKs). Launch gates: docs + 2 beta customers + perf targets met."

sdkbot: deploy-notify: created draft doc at https://intern.docs/redwood/streaming/2364129876 (private).

jordan_cs: Thanks — please ping when draft is public, I'll loop customers.

maria_pm: Will do. Closing thread once handoffs are in the trackers. :white_check_mark:
